newsitem.title: QATAR: Qatar budget sees higher 97/98 spending, revenue.
newsitem.headline: Qatar budget sees higher 97/98 spending, revenue.

text.p: Qatar on Sunday announced a 1997/98 budget projecting higher spending of 16.38 billion riyals ($4.5 billion) and increased revenue of 13.39 billion on a slightly higher deficit of 2.98 billion, the Finance Ministry said.
The ministry statement, carried by the official Qatari news agency, said the budget runs from April 1.
The 1996/97 deficit was 2.95 billion riyals on spending of 13.75 billion and revenue of 10.80 billion.

The ministry statement did not say what oil price the budget was based on, but Qatar's Energy and Industry Minister Abdullah bin Hamad al-Attiyah said on March 19 the OPEC producer would base its 97/98 budget at $16 a barrel of oil, up 40 cents from the last financial year.

Qatar receives about 70 percent of its state revenues from oil sales and the rest from hydrocarbon-based industries. In the 1997/98 financial year, Qatar coffers will be boosted by higher oil output and revenues from its Qatargas LNG plant.
The statement said the budget was part of government plans to wipe out the deficit by the year 2000, diversify the economy and increase public income.
